images.title: Average daylight per day in two cities
images.purpose: Show the clustered column graph of average daylight hours per day in two cities, month by month.
images.composition: One clustered column graph, months along the bottom, hours up the side, legend at the top.
exact_structure: A vertical axis from 0 to 20 with numbered gridlines at 0, 5, 10, 15 and 20 (scale 1 unit = 5 hours), captioned Number of hours per day.
Twelve month groups labelled Jan to Dec, each with two columns: amber (#E69F00) for City 1 on the left and teal (#0072B2) for City 2 on the right.
A legend at the top: an amber square labelled City 1 and a teal square labelled City 2. No values printed on the columns.
labels: Average daylight hours in two cities
rejection: the two cities' patterns not mirror images
images.takeaway: When one city has its longest days the other has its shortest, so they lie on opposite sides of the equator.
images.description: A clustered column graph of daylight hours per day in two cities across the year.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Ask which month is longest for each city and what that suggests about where the cities are.

image_decisions.why: The pattern across months is only visible in the clustered graph.
